name: Korean pine (红松, Pinus koraiensis)
summary: A light, soft, resinous white pine of north-east China, Korea and the Russian Far East. In Chenghuai it is the columns, beams and all the lattice, and it is never seen bare: every member is wrapped in a lime-and-hemp ground (地仗) and oil-painted iron-oxide red, black or green, or painted in the Suzhou manner.

class.text: Softwood (vessels absent); normal resin canals, axial and radial, large and diffuse; growth-ring boundaries distinct with a gradual earlywood-latewood transition; rays narrow; resinous odour.
class.source: Richter, H.G., Gembruch, K. & Koch, G. (2014 onwards) CITESwoodID: Pinus koraiensis (Korea-Kiefer, Korean pine), version 4 April 2023, https://www.delta-intkey.com/citeswood/en/www/pinpinko.htm

whyAnAccent.text: Principle 2 names one oak. Chenghuai is built as it would be in Beijing, and its approved Materials board names Korean pine, Chinese fir and plantation Phoebe. Each is declared an accent of the oak family (D-014): timber in the oak's role, tied to it by value and hue under its finish. The Architect may overturn this reading.
whyAnAccent.source: MuseeVision/Journal/Decisions.md, D-014 (Matter: every substance carries its family; an accent names its core family); plan/proposals/chenghuai/canvas/Materials.dc.html (approved Chenghuai proposal: '營造')

formation.how: A five-needle white pine of cold mixed forest. Its wood is even-textured, with a gradual change from earlywood to latewood, large resin canals and a heartwood that turns brown, red or yellow, distinct from the sapwood. Soft, light and easily worked, it takes the carpenter's joints and, under the ground, the painter's work.

fibreHighlight.text: Finished wood shows a subsurface highlight that no surface-anisotropy model reproduces: light enters, scatters from the aligned fibres below the surface and leaves on a cone about the local fibre axis, which can tilt out of the surface plane. The model adds a fibre term (fibre axis u, fibre colour k_f, and a Gaussian highlight width beta, one per species) to a Fresnel-corrected diffuse term and the finish's own surface specular; both subsurface terms are attenuated by Fresnel transmission in and out through the finish. On interlocked grain the highlight swings 30-40 degrees either side of the normal across the figure. Measured samples: varnished walnut, lacquered walnut, lacquered curly maple, varnished padauk; oak was not measured.

photograph: No bare pine shows. Under the red paint, fine checks along the grain of big columns telegraph through the ground as hairline cracks.
A column is slightly tapered (收分) and its paint wraps it without joints; the ground rounds every arris.

evidenceSearch.found: Nothing: no pine set on this PC, and none is needed while every pine surface is painted.
evidenceSearch.tier: The painted surface is calibrated through the workings' pigments and films (tier a) and a painted specimen (tier b).

unverified.reason: The Materials board gives the garden's finish (栗壳色 广漆) but not its timber; Korean pine and Chinese fir are the board's two structural timbers. The Architect should name it.
The measured values are for plantation trees grown in Korea; old-growth north-east Chinese timber, the historic Beijing supply, may be denser.
Not sourced; the pine is not walked on.
